entries.catalyst: Jensen Huang testifies before the Senate Banking Committee Wed 3 Dec 2026 (Bloomberg, reported 25 Nov 2026); post-Thanksgiving seasonal window noted by McMillan/MarketWatch 25 Nov
entries.thesis: TRADED LEVELS (operator override, 25 Nov 09:00 ET: buy at the lower price instead of waiting for the 151-156 reclaim) - entry zone 144.00-146.00, stop 141.00, target 156.00. NVIDIA has gone from a leadership shock to a valuation floor in nine sessions: 239.24 on 6 Oct to 125.53 on 20 Nov (-47.5%), then +31.5% on 23 Nov when the board re-hired Jensen Huang, then -5.9% on 24 Nov to 155.38, and 146.04 in the 25 Nov premarket while the whole AI complex is down 3-5% on a reported tariff threat to 16 trading partners and a core PCE print of 3.3% y/y, the highest since Nov 2023. The desk is not buying the fall. It buys only if the price reclaims the 24 Nov low of 150.50 and trades back into 151-156, which is the level the 24 Nov close left and the level the bounce has to hold for the 23 Nov reversal to mean anything. Fundamentally the stock trades near 10x forward earnings, its cheapest multiple since 2008 and the lowest of the Mag-7, after at least three sell-side upgrades since the re-hire with targets of 220 (Goldman), 220 (UBS), 240 (Citi) and 270 (StoneX); the mean target implies about +57% over twelve months. That is the case for owning a recovery rather than chasing one: the entry is a level, the stop is 148 (under the 24 Nov low, so a failed reclaim is out for 2-5%), the target 172 is a retest of the 23 Nov high of 171.50, and 172 against a 156 top-of-zone entry is 2.0 reward per unit of risk, above the lane's 1.5 floor.
entries.synthesis: Two axes agree and two disagree, so the plan is conditional instead of immediate: valuation and sentiment lean up, trend and fund flows lean down, and the only honest way to trade that split is to let the market prove the support first by reclaiming 150.50-151.00.
entries.edge: The lane's edge here is discipline, not forecast: the desk buys a defined level with a defined stop, sizes so a stop-out costs 0.53% of NAV, and holds for a scheduled catalyst rather than a chart. A swing hold is what makes that possible at all, because the reclaim may come a day or two after the entry is reviewed.
entries.bear_case: The 25 Nov premarket is a broad AI de-rating (MSFT -3.3%, GOOGL -4.5%, META -2.1%, AMZN -3.4%), not an NVIDIA story, so a reclaim can fail on tape. The Scout capture has NVDA at rank 3, conviction medium, stance watch, with heavy sector outflows, insider selling and price 17% under its 20-day average; the tariff headline and the hearing can both go against the stock, and the 8-K and Form 4 filings of 24-25 Nov show the governance story is unresolved.
entries.invalidation: Stop 141.00 (under the 25 Nov premarket low), target 156.00, or the hold-by date. A close below 150.50 with the reclaim never taken means the 23 Nov reversal was a dead-cat bounce: no entry. If filled, the plan is wrong below 148, and the Scout capture's own test, price back above SMA20 175.78, is not met today, so this entry buys support rather than a trend.
entries.horizon: Swing: held to the 4 Dec 2026 hold-by date, or its stop, target, or invalidation, whichever comes first. 3 Dec testimony falls inside the hold; 2 Dec is the alternative hold-by if the operator prefers to sit the hearing out.

entries.catalyst: Same thesis as NVDA-20261125-SWING: the 3 Dec Senate testimony and the post-Thanksgiving window; this leg only has to prove the option plumbing inside the challenge window
entries.thesis: TRADED LEVELS (operator override, 25 Nov 09:00 ET: buy at the lower price instead of waiting for the 151-156 reclaim) - entry zone 144.00-146.00, stop 141.00, target 156.00. The same NVIDIA thesis as the share plan, expressed with one long call so the loss is capped at the premium. NVDA 18 Dec 150 call (US.NVDA261218C150000) printed 9.55 on 25 Nov after a 10.20-10.30 open, on 109 contracts and 22,950 open interest, with delta 0.49, implied volatility 76.2% and 23 days to expiry; the 14.209 previous settlement shows how much premium the -5.9% 24 Nov day took out. It is the only tactical contract that clears this lane's own filters: the 4 Dec and 11 Dec weeklies fail the volume floor (29 and 30 contracts on 24 Nov) and the 155 and 160 strikes fail the 0.45 delta floor. One contract at about 9.55 is roughly $955 plus fees, which fits the 1.5% per-trade premium budget (about $1,482) and the 5% aggregate cap.
entries.synthesis: Buying the option instead of the shares here is the test, not the bet: same levels, same thesis, a known maximum loss, and the desk's first proof that an option can be planned, approved, filled, protected and closed on this account.
entries.edge: Time-boxed and small: the hold-by date is Fri 27 Nov, the last session of the challenge window, so this leg cannot become a stranded position. The lane's exit rules sell at the bid if the underlying hits 148 or 172, if the premium falls 40% from the fill, or at 12:10 ET on 27 Nov, whichever comes first.
entries.bear_case: The call is at the money against a falling tape: at a 146.04 premarket the 150 strike is out of the money and delta 0.49 sits only just above the 0.45 floor, so if NVDA keeps sliding the contract stops qualifying before it loses more. Implied vol of 76% is expensive, theta is about -0.25 per day, and a flat three days costs roughly 2.5 points of the 9.55.
entries.invalidation: Stop 141.00 (under the 25 Nov premarket low), target 156.00, or the hold-by date. Per the lane: underlying at 148, the option's bid at 60% of the price paid, the share thesis invalidated, or the 27 Nov deadline. Under the operator ruling of 24 Nov this option does not wait for the underlying to enter the 151-156 zone - the first in-session run that finds the contract inside the liquidity filter buys it, so on a down morning it can be bought below the share zone. Turn PB-003 off before the 09:30 open if that is not wanted today.
entries.horizon: Two sessions: bought on 25 Nov, sold by 12:10 ET Fri 27 Nov, or earlier on its stop, target or 40% premium drawdown. The contract itself expires 18 Dec, outside the window, so it can never be exercised or expire inside the test.

entries.catalyst: No KO-specific event in the window. The driver is the tape: BNP Paribas raised its KO price target to 107 from 102 on 25 Nov (MT Newswires, 05:30 ET), and the Street average of 100.14 sits just above the 24 Nov close.
entries.thesis: Money is rotating out of the AI complex and into staples on the same tape that knocked 5.9% off NVIDIA on 24 Nov: KO closed 97.62, up 1.81% on the day NVDA fell 5.86%, and it trades 98.19 in the 25 Nov premarket - 1.9% above its 20-day average of 96.33 and only 2.4% below its all-time high of 100.56. The 23 Nov low of 94.60 has now held twice (19 Nov low 94.73), so the pullback has a floor under it and the breakout has a ceiling above it that is 2.4% away. The desk buys the floor, not the ceiling: entry 96.80-98.30, stop 94.40 under both swing lows, target 105.00 for a move through the old high.
entries.synthesis: Long 100 Coca-Cola shares as a defensive-rotation swing to 4 Dec. This is the operator's own 23 Nov thesis (risk-off into staples and healthcare, long only) with the tape finally agreeing, and it diversifies a book that is currently all NVIDIA.
entries.edge: (105.00 - 98.30) / (98.30 - 94.40) = 1.72 reward per unit of risk, above the lane's 1.5 floor, and the stop is 2.0 times KO's own 14-day average range of 1.94 rather than an arbitrary round number. A full stop-out costs about 0.39% of NAV, well inside the 1% per-trade risk budget.
entries.bear_case: KO is not cheap on any measure: 32.1 trailing PE, 28.8 PE TTM, price to book 11.2, and the Street's average target of 100.14 is only 2.6% above the last close, so there is no valuation cushion if the rotation reverses. The 24 Nov rise came on 21.6M shares, a volume ratio of 0.909, i.e. below average participation, and a risk-on snap-back after the holiday would take the bid out of staples first.
entries.invalidation: A regular close below 94.60 means the twice-held floor has gone and the rotation is over: exit at the 94.40 stop. If the price runs above 98.30 without filling the zone, the entry is skipped rather than chased, and the 4 Dec hold-by date closes the trade regardless of price.
entries.horizon: Swing: held across sessions to 4 Dec 2026, or its stop, or its target, whichever comes first. Never closed because a session ended.
